text:
Mia: quick note — I ran an apples-to-apples comparison between kernel-selector=cost and kernel-selector=latency on the same replay seed and saw weird p95 discrepancies when KV cache is enabled.
Devin: can you paste the exact run command and the perf numbers?
Mia: command: `./bench/run --workload apples_v3 --seed 1337 --selector=cost --kv-cache=on --batcher=continuous --concurrency=24`
Mia: baseline (selector=latency, kv=off): p50=18ms p95=54ms p99=120ms
Mia: test (selector=cost, kv=on): p50=22ms p95=74ms p99=210ms — noticed KV hit-rate starts low and ramps over ~30s which skews the CI nightly summary (single-run).
Sasha: interesting — so CI is flagging the single nightly run as a regression because the test warmup was different? :thinking_face:
PerfBot: nightly-bench: regression detected on eng-runtime/apples_v3 (p95 +37% vs baseline). Run id: nightly/2024-12-05-03. Alert: #perf-alerts.
Devin: this smells like harness-level non-determinism — replays can produce different tokenization/prefix alignment causing KV miss patterns. Did you compare replay vs synthetic?
Mia: yes — synthetic loadshape (token-length-normalized) keeps KV warm and p95 stays within 5% across selectors. Replay shows the ramp.
ReplayHarnessBot: note: replay harness currently replays user traces as-is (no kvcache prewarm).
Jules: we should make apples-to-apples include a deterministic KV prewarm phase for replay runs so the steady-state numbers are comparable to synthetic. Also run 3 repeats and take median before thresholding.
Ram: agree. Another option: change CI threshold to compute trimmed mean over N runs and ignore first 20s of samples (warmup window).
Sasha: pros/cons: prewarm masks user-observed startup cost; trim-window ignores transient but may hide real regressions in cold-start scenarios. For our use-case (inference steady-state), steady-state matters more.
Devin: proposal: in nightly job, run two subjobs: (1) replay-with-prewarm -> steady-state metrics, (2) synthetic-loadshape -> stress/corner behaviors. Both publish to dashboard. Thresholds use replay-with-prewarm median over 3 runs.
Mia: implemented a local patch to prewarm by replaying first 60s of trace with faster token injection: `--prewarm=60 --prewarm-speed=10x` and then collect 5m steady-state. Results look stable.
Jules: please open an ENG task for CI changes (prewarm + repeats + trimmed-mean). Also add a kvcache_hit_rate series to the bench metrics and expose in the apples dashboard.
Mia: opened ENG-1124: "ci: apples replay prewarm + median-of-3 + kvcache metrics" — PR coming. Link: https://redwood.internal/ENG-1124
PerfBot: perf-bot: new dashboard artifact uploaded: s3://bench-artifacts/nightly/1746523456/apples_v3/ — panels: p50/p95/p99, kvcache_hit_rate, selector_comparison.
Ram: small caveat — kernel selection sometimes prefers larger kernel for batched paths; when kvcache misses spike, compute path changes and we get different memory access pattern -> p99 blowups. We should capture kernel_id distribution in metrics.
Devin: add `kernel_id` histogram to infra metric set. We already have an exporter; just need to wire the selector to emit chosen kernel per request.
Sasha: for flaky triage: create a CI annotation that attaches the three raw run artifacts and a short summary to the nightly alert: `regression? yes/no`, `variance`, `kvcache_ramp_seconds`. That'll speed triage.
Jules: assigning: I'll do the CI job changes + dashboard binding. Mia — can you add the prewarm flag to the replay harness? Devin — can you add kernel_id metrics? Ram — can you prototype a small kprobe-based trace to validate kernel memory path on p99 events?
Mia: yes, will PR prewarm by EOD.
Devin: will add kernel_id export tomorrow.
Ram: will sketch the kprobe script and run on a repro cluster.
Sasha: thanks all. Once ENG-1124 PRs land we'll roll out to nightly and reduce false positives. Also adding a short note in the bench docs about "why single-run nightly is insufficient for kvcache-sensitive workloads."
Mia: quick snippet of the warmup guard I'm adding to harness if helpful: ```
# prewarm replay harness
for t in seq 1 $PREWARM_SECONDS; do
  inject_next_trace_token --speed $PREWARM_SPEED
done
sleep 1
start_collecting_metrics
```
Jules: looks good. Please also include a tiny repro script to reproduce the regression — makes triage trivial.
PerfBot: nightly-bench: re-run scheduled after PR merge. :white_check_mark:
Mia: thanks — will follow up with the PR number once ready.
